title: Aggregate

validation.research: Evans's original accessible DDD Reference, Aggregates on printed page 16, establishes a root, whole-unit invariants, controlled references, and transaction boundaries. Fowler distinguishes domain aggregates from generic collections and UML aggregation. Vernon, Effective Aggregate Design Part I, supports real invariants, small consistency boundaries, loading/contention costs, and one-aggregate transactions as a design goal requiring analysis. Microsoft's domain-model guidance supports root-controlled updates and identity references; official EF Core concurrency documentation supports conditional version checks, stale-write failure, and conflict handling. Python documents frozen-field behavior. Aggregate root is identified as a role, rather than aliased to every object in the boundary. SQL aggregate functions and analytics summaries are explicitly separate meanings. The load-plan policy, code, and native SVGs are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual Python article blocks execute together and produce all five output lines exactly. Checks cover positive exact-integer kilogram inputs, Boolean/fractional/text/zero/negative rejection, nonblank opaque text identifiers, constructor validation, empty valid plans, exact-capacity acceptance, capacity excess on addition or replacement without mutation, replacement rather than duplicate accumulation, repeated setting without increments, stable root identity, immutable tuples and frozen allocation fields, earlier snapshots retained through later changes, separate plans referencing the same package without claiming global uniqueness, and arbitrarily large integer unit counts. An independent dictionary oracle checks every intermediate accepted/rejected state in 1875 bounded four-command sequences. A separate sequential trace verifies the illustrated version-7/version-8 conflict and rejection after re-evaluation; it is explicitly not a persistence or atomic compare-and-swap implementation. The model imports only dataclasses and performs no I/O.

example_limits: One sequential in-memory LoadPlan root owns immutable Allocation values. It models only positive integer kilograms and a combined weight limit; it does not model vehicle safety, volume, axle distribution, route ordering, package existence, global exclusive assignment, root-ID allocation, persistence, transaction rollback, authorization, or competing writers. Underscore fields and frozen dataclasses protect normal API use, not deliberate runtime bypass. The separate version diagram and ordered validation trace describe a required persistent concurrency protocol; storage must provide atomic expected-version comparison, all member writes, and token advancement. A root-row token is effective only when every child-writing path participates. Cross-aggregate messages, duplicate handling, ordering, and external-effect delivery require additional designs.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
